paper: Mohr T, Aliyu H, Kuchlin R, et al. (2018) Comparative genomic analysis of Parageobacillus thermoglucosidasius strains with distinct hydrogenogenic capacities. BMC Genomics 19:880.

open_questions.q: Is the CO-dependent water-gas-shift (CODH + NiFe/FHL hydrogenase) locus architecture conserved as a discrete genomic island across the wider Parageobacillus thermoglucosidasius species pan-genome, or is its presence in DSM 2543 / 6285 / 21625 vs. absence in DSM 2542T a lineage-specific accessory-genome event?
open_questions.basis: The rerun reproduces the locus presence/polymorphism pattern in exactly the four strains the paper studied (2 CO-DH + 10 NiFe/FHL hits in the three hydrogenogenic strains vs. 1 CO-DH + 0 NiFe/FHL in DSM 2542T), but four strains is too few to distinguish clade-wide conservation from mobile-element / horizontal acquisition. Mohr et al. inferred a mechanism but did not survey the species broadly.
next_steps: Pull all publicly available P. thermoglucosidasius assemblies from NCBI/BV-BRC (well beyond the four used here).
Run prokka on each and count CODH + NiFe/FHL hydrogenase product hits, mirroring the presence/absence proxy used in this rerun.
Perform synteny analysis (e.g., Mauve or clinker) across the CODH-hydrogenase region to test whether flanks look conserved (vertical) or bounded by mobile-genetic-element signatures (horizontal).
Correlate locus content with any reported H2-production phenotypes in strain metadata.

open_questions.q: In thermophilic Parageobacillus fermentation, what is the quantitative trade-off between H2 yield and organic-acid (acetate, lactate, formate) accumulation, and can it be re-engineered without collapsing growth?
open_questions.basis: The paper (and this rerun) establish that CODH-NiFe-hydrogenase presence is necessary for the H2 phenotype, but neither addresses the metabolic-flux consequence: diverting reducing equivalents to H2 competes with organic-acid pathways. The genomic evidence is silent on yield engineering.
next_steps: Build a genome-scale metabolic model (e.g., via CobraPy / carveme) for DSM 2543 using the prokka annotations already produced.
Run flux-balance analysis with H2 as objective vs. biomass as objective; map the Pareto frontier for H2 vs. acetate / lactate / formate.
Cross-reference in silico gene-knockout candidates (e.g., ldh, pflB homologs) against essentiality predictions before proposing wet-lab targets.
Compare predictions to any published chemostat or batch-fermentation yield data for the four strains.

open_questions.q: Is biological H2 production by Parageobacillus thermoglucosidasius scalable to industrially relevant volumes and productivities, given thermophilic operation and CO-tolerance requirements?
open_questions.basis: Mohr et al. is a comparative-genomics paper; it identifies the locus responsible for the phenotype but does not address bioreactor economics, CO-mass-transfer limits, or downstream H2 recovery. The rerun equally cannot speak to scale-up.
next_steps: Literature review of existing bench-scale (mL-L) and pilot-scale (>10 L) fermentations of P. thermoglucosidasius or closely related thermophiles reporting H2 productivity and yield.
Techno-economic analysis (TEA) comparing biological water-gas-shift H2 to conventional catalytic WGS at matched CO input purities.
Assess gas-mass-transfer bottlenecks (kLa) for CO delivery at 60-65 C operating temperature.
Identify which of the four strains has the most tractable growth kinetics for scale-up (may be independent of raw H2 yield).

open_questions.q: How does the CODH-NiFe-hydrogenase repertoire of P. thermoglucosidasius compare with related Geobacillus and Parageobacillus species (e.g., G. thermoleovorans, G. kaustophilus, P. toebii), and does hydrogenogenic capacity map cleanly onto the phylogeny?
open_questions.basis: The paper stays within P. thermoglucosidasius. Whether the hydrogenogenic trait is genus-wide, sub-clade-specific, or scattered by horizontal transfer is unresolved. This directly affects any 'chassis selection' argument for biological H2 production.
next_steps: Build a curated set of Geobacillus/Parageobacillus reference genomes from NCBI.
Compute a species tree (e.g., GTDB-Tk placement or a marker-gene phylogeny).
Annotate each genome with prokka and count CODH / NiFe / FHL hydrogenase hits with the same proxy pipeline used here.
Paint the trait onto the tree and test whether presence maps to monophyletic clades or is patchy (suggestive of HGT).

open_questions.q: How is the hyc-like (formate-hydrogenlyase / NiFe-hydrogenase) gene cluster regulated in P. thermoglucosidasius under CO exposure and H2 accumulation, and are the regulatory elements conserved among the three hydrogenogenic strains?
open_questions.basis: The rerun and the paper both identify the structural gene complement but neither addresses regulation. Yet CO-sensing regulators (e.g., CooA homologs) and H2-feedback regulation could explain per-strain differences in hydrogenogenic rate even when structural genes are all present.
next_steps: Search prokka annotations for CooA / other CO-sensing transcription factor homologs upstream of the hyc-like cluster in all four strains.
Perform MEME/FIMO motif analysis on the intergenic regions upstream of the CODH-hydrogenase operon across strains to test cis-regulatory conservation.
Design an RNA-seq experiment (CO-shifted vs. control) on at least one hydrogenogenic strain and DSM 2542T as a comparator.
Cross-reference candidate regulators against known Geobacillus/Bacillus regulatory-network databases to prioritize experimental follow-up.
